name: Immunovex
subcategory: immune modulator for the heavily augmented
description: Immunovex is an advanced immunological balancing agent designed for individuals with extensive cybernetic augmentation, where the immune system must simultaneously tolerate large volumes of synthetic material while still defending against genuine pathogens. Standard rejection suppressors create too broad an immunosuppression for heavily augmented individuals, leaving them dangerously vulnerable to infection. Immunovex uses a selective checkpoint modulation approach that maintains pathogen response while establishing durable tolerance to implant materials.
effects: selective immunological tolerance of cybernetic implants without broad immunosuppression
reduced incidence of opportunistic infections in heavily augmented users
stabilization of immune function across high-chrome-density implant zones
reduced systemic inflammation from implant-immune interface
side_effects: complex dosing requirements — miscalibration can tip toward either rejection or immunosuppression
requires regular blood work to monitor immune profile
expensive and requires specialist physician management
rare autoimmune flares if dosing lapses
not compatible with some older augment alloy formulations
can reduce vaccine efficacy — requires adjusted vaccination protocols
cultural_context: Immunovex is the drug that separates the moderately augmented from the heavily chromed. Anyone running military-grade augmentation loads, full-limb replacements, or extensive internal chrome needs Immunovex rather than standard rejection suppressors. It's expensive enough that Tier 2 users with heavy aug loads are often undermedicated, running on cheaper broad suppressors and hoping they don't catch anything serious. Tier 4-5 heavy aug users have it delivered by medical courier and managed by personal physicians. Among the chromed elite, the quality of your Immunovex protocol is a status signal.
story_hooks: A Tier 2 heavy-aug enforcer has been making do with standard rejection suppressors, and a minor infection is turning catastrophic — they need Immunovex they can't afford, and someone is using that leverage to coerce them into a job.

A batch of Immunovex has been contaminated with a compound that subtly tips the immune balance toward rejection — the first symptoms look like a normal infection, and by the time the rejection cascade becomes obvious, the damage is severe.

Helix Biosystems has developed an Immunovex formulation that also suppresses the neurological markers of fear and moral conflict — and someone at a Tier 5 level is funding its distribution to a private military contractor's heavily augmented personnel.
